stubs.angle: How does a parent component pass a value to a child component, and what must the child declare to receive it?
stubs.answerHinge: The child exposes a public property marked with [Parameter], and the parent sets it as an attribute with the same name in its markup.

stubs.angle: Why does an EditForm whose model has [Required] attributes submit without any validation messages?
stubs.answerHinge: EditForm checks DataAnnotations attributes only when a DataAnnotationsValidator component is placed inside it; without it, the attributes are ignored.

stubs.angle: Find the line that throws when a prerendered InteractiveServer component calls IJSRuntime in OnInitializedAsync.
stubs.answerHinge: During prerendering there is no browser connection, so JS interop calls fail; they belong in OnAfterRenderAsync when firstRender is true.

stubs.angle: Why does a prerendered interactive component load its data twice and show a flicker, and how do you avoid it?
stubs.answerHinge: With prerendering the component is created once for the static HTML and again when it becomes interactive, so OnInitializedAsync runs twice unless state is carried over with PersistentComponentState or prerendering is disabled.

stubs.angle: Why does the parent re-render after a child invokes an EventCallback parameter but not after it invokes an Action parameter?
stubs.answerHinge: EventCallback dispatches through the receiving component's IHandleEvent, so ComponentBase calls StateHasChanged on the parent; a plain Action delegate bypasses that.

stubs.angle: In a .NET 8 or later Blazor Web App a page renders but its @onclick button does nothing; what is the most likely cause?
stubs.answerHinge: A component with no render mode and no global interactivity is rendered with static SSR, which produces plain HTML with no event handlers attached.

stubs.angle: Which statements about ProtectedLocalStorage and ProtectedSessionStorage are true?
stubs.answerHinge: They encrypt data with ASP.NET Core Data Protection on the server, work only in server-side interactive rendering, are asynchronous and cannot be used during prerendering.

stubs.angle: Which statements about OnSubmit, OnValidSubmit, Model and EditContext on an EditForm are true?
stubs.answerHinge: OnValidSubmit runs only after validation passes, OnSubmit requires calling EditContext.Validate yourself, and combining OnSubmit with OnValidSubmit or Model with EditContext throws.

stubs.angle: An InteractiveServer app runs out of memory and drops users as concurrent sessions grow; how do you diagnose and fix it?
stubs.answerHinge: Every circuit keeps its component tree and scoped services in server memory, including retained disconnected circuits, so you shrink per-circuit state, tune circuit retention, scale out with sticky sessions and measure memory per circuit.

stubs.angle: Find the line that leaks memory when a component passes DotNetObjectReference.Create(this) to JavaScript in OnAfterRenderAsync.
stubs.answerHinge: A DotNetObjectReference keeps the .NET object alive until it is disposed, so creating one on every render without a firstRender check and without Dispose leaks references.

stubs.angle: Why does a child component re-render every time its parent re-renders even though the object passed as its parameter did not change?
stubs.answerHinge: ComponentBase skips re-rendering only when all parameters are of known immutable primitive types with unchanged values; any parameter of a complex type is treated as possibly changed.

stubs.angle: Which pieces are required for an EditForm on a static SSR page in .NET 8 or later to post and bind its model?
stubs.answerHinge: The form needs a FormName, the model property needs [SupplyParameterFromForm], and the pipeline needs antiforgery middleware; an interactive render mode is not required.

stubs.angle: How do you design data access for a component that runs in InteractiveAuto mode?
stubs.answerHinge: The same component first runs on the server and later in WebAssembly, so it depends on an interface with a server implementation that uses the database directly and a client implementation that calls a web API over HttpClient.

stubs.angle: Which user state survives a page reload, a new tab or a long network drop in an InteractiveServer app, and where should state live that must survive them?
stubs.answerHinge: In-memory circuit state lives only as long as the circuit, so a reload, a new tab or an expired disconnected circuit loses it; durable state goes to a database, browser storage or the URL.

stubs.angle: What happens to an InteractiveServer circuit when a component throws, and what can and cannot ErrorBoundary contain?
stubs.answerHinge: An unhandled exception is fatal to the circuit; ErrorBoundary catches exceptions from rendering and lifecycle methods of its child content but not exceptions from code outside the renderer such as timer callbacks.

stubs.angle: Which statements about JavaScript interop in the InteractiveServer render mode are true?
stubs.answerHinge: Every interop call is an asynchronous round trip over SignalR, IJSInProcessRuntime is not available, and large payloads are limited by the hub message size, so streams are used for big data.

stubs.angle: A Blazor Web App has public content pages and an admin area, and the team argues about global versus per-page interactivity; how do you decide and set the rule?
stubs.answerHinge: Per-page or per-component interactivity keeps content pages as cheap static SSR without circuits or WebAssembly downloads, while global interactivity is needed only when layout components must be interactive everywhere.

stubs.angle: Several teams want a shared Blazor component library; which rules and process do you set so it stays usable for years?
stubs.answerHinge: Components in a Razor class library must not assume a render mode or hosting model, ship with versioning and a deprecation policy, and keep CSS and JS isolated, so consumers can upgrade independently.

stubs.angle: What team policy do you set for using third-party JavaScript libraries from Blazor components?
stubs.answerHinge: Each library is wrapped once in a typed C# service or component that loads an isolated JS module, disposes its object references and works in every render mode, instead of scattered string-named interop calls.

stubs.angle: Validation rules for WebAssembly forms and the backing API have drifted apart and caused bad data; what do you change?
stubs.answerHinge: Client validation in WebAssembly is only a convenience because the code runs on the user's machine, so the API must validate every request, and rules are shared from one library used by both sides.

stubs.angle: An InteractiveServer app built for one office must now serve users on several continents; how do you redesign hosting and render modes?
stubs.answerHinge: InteractiveServer pays network latency on every UI event and needs a live connection to the region holding the circuit, so for distant users you move interaction to WebAssembly or static SSR and deploy per region.

stubs.angle: How do you decide between Blazor and a JavaScript SPA framework for a product expected to live many years?
stubs.answerHinge: The decision weighs shared C# code and team skills against WebAssembly download size, the ecosystem of UI components and the hiring market, and it is made per product surface rather than for the whole company.
